mandatoryEscalationRules.rationale: Webhook/messaging change requires provider suite, persistence suite, idempotency suite (messagingInboundIdempotency.ts owner tests), safety suite (msg-safety), and tenant-scope suite together.

KVKK/privacy change requires privacy suite, role/permission suite, tenant suite, audit suite (even though AUD has 0 owned tests today - this rule mandates AUD-adjacent assertions inside PRV/consumer suites run), retention suite, and export/anonymization suite as applicable.

Payment/financial change requires billing-access, validation, calculation, and receipt/report regression suites together - RISK_REGISTER.md has no dedicated Payments risk row, which this design treats as a coverage gap, not a reason to narrow scope (see RISK_REGISTER.md R-072).

mandatoryEscalationRules.trigger: Any file under server/src/{routes/imaging*.ts,services/imaging/**,routes/attachments.ts,services/fileStorage.ts} or bridge-agent/**, windows-bridge/**.
mandatoryEscalationRules.rationale: Storage/imaging change requires metadata, authorization, upload/download/delete, and rollback/restore-adjacent tests (per the F0-011 backup/restore gap matrix) together.

AI change requires deterministic safety/regression evaluation (existing msg-safety suite) plus fallback-behavior tests - RISK_REGISTER.md R-014 (hallucination) and R-066 (fragile JSON parsing) both name this exact code path.

mandatoryEscalationRules.trigger: Any change to this design's own future CI implementation (test-selection engine code/config itself, once it exists) or to server/package.json's test-script chain.
mandatoryEscalationRules.rationale: A test-selection engine change is the one category that can silently reduce coverage everywhere; it must run the full suite until independently re-verified, per this task's own required design principle (item K, auditability).

phase1.name: Shadow computation, full suite still authoritative
actions: Compute the selected test scope for every PR.
Still run the full suite (S4-equivalent) on every PR, unchanged from today's manual/local practice.
Record predicted-scope vs. which suites actually failed, without acting on the prediction.
phase1.exitCriteria: At least 50 real PRs recorded with zero implementation changes to the selector logic during the window.

phase2.name: False-negative/false-positive metric collection
actions: Compute falseNegativeRate, missedFailingSuiteCount, selectedSuitePrecision, selectedSuiteRecall per PR.
Publish a rolling report; no CI behavior changes yet.
phase2.exitCriteria: falseNegativeRate == 0 for every PR touching a CRITICAL-risk dimension across the full phase-2 window, with zero exceptions; sustained over at least 100 PRs or 30 days, whichever is longer.

phase3.name: Reduced execution for low-risk classes only
actions: Allow the selector to actually skip suites, but only for changes classified LOW risk with HIGH confidence (CT-01, CT-02, CT-03 taxonomy categories).
Every other risk tier still runs S4 regardless of prediction.
A one-switch environment/config flag reverts to phase-2 (shadow-only) behavior instantly.
phase3.exitCriteria: Zero missed failures attributable to a skipped suite for LOW-risk changes across the full phase-3 window; MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL changes show unchanged 100% full-suite execution.

phase4.name: Cautious expansion with rollback switch
actions: Expand reduced execution to MEDIUM-risk, HIGH-confidence changes only, one taxonomy category at a time, each requiring its own separate task authorization (not granted in bulk by this design).
CRITICAL-risk and LOW-confidence/UNKNOWN changes never leave full-suite execution under this design - that boundary is not something phase 4 is authorized to cross.
phase4.exitCriteria: Defined per expanded category at the time of its own authorization task; this design pre-commits only to the falseNegativeRate == 0 requirement for CRITICAL-risk changes never being relaxed at any phase.

falseNegativeRate.definition: Fraction of PRs where a suite NOT selected by the predictor would have failed if run. Acceptable rate for HIGH/CRITICAL-risk changes: 0 (zero), permanently, at every phase.
falseNegativeRate.acceptableForNonHighRisk: Tracked but not gated below phase 3; phase 3 itself requires 0 for the LOW-risk class it activates on.

missedFailingSuiteCount.definition: Absolute count (not rate) of suites that failed but were excluded from the selected scope, per rolling window.

selectedSuitePrecision.definition: Of the suites selected, the fraction that were actually relevant (touched code the change affected) - a low-relevance selector wastes CI time even without missing failures.

selectedSuiteRecall.definition: Of the suites that should have run (touched code the change affected, whether or not they failed), the fraction actually selected.

averageRuntimeSaved.definition: Mean wall-clock reduction versus always running S4, measured only once phase 3 begins skipping suites.

highRiskOverrideFrequency.definition: How often a mandatoryEscalationRules/fullSuiteTriggers rule fires and overrides a narrower taxonomy default - a rising trend signals the taxonomy defaults are miscalibrated, not that the overrides are wrong.

unknownOwnershipFrequency.definition: How often ESC-01 (UNKNOWN confidence) fires - a rising trend signals TEST_OWNERSHIP.md/F0-005 evidence is going stale faster than it is refreshed (see RISK_REGISTER.md R-072).

staleGraphDetectionFrequency.definition: How often the confidenceModel.stalenessThreshold condition fires - directly measures whether the evidence-refresh cadence a future implementation adopts is keeping pace with repository change velocity.

rollbackDesign.oneSwitchFallback: A single boolean config/environment flag (name/location to be defined by the implementation task, not this design) that, when set, forces every PR to S4 regardless of any classification - this is the same one-switch-to-full-suite pattern already implicit in this program's existing production kill-switch precedents (e.g. privacy.legacyConsentCorrection.runtimeEnabled).
rollbackDesign.noDestructiveMigration: This design introduces no schema, migration, or data change of any kind - the rollback of a future implementation is a code/config revert only.
rollbackDesign.noDependencyOnUnavailableGraphService: The design's evidence sources (F0-003/F0-004/F0-005-equivalent JSON) are static, repository-committed artifacts, not a live service call - a future implementation that instead queries a live dependency-graph tool (e.g. CodeGraph) at CI time MUST fail closed to S4 if that tool is unavailable or times out, never fail open to a narrower scope.
rollbackDesign.defaultFullSuiteOnSelectorFailure: Any selector exception, timeout, malformed input, or unrecognized file path MUST default to S4, not S0/S1 - 'no tests selected' is never an acceptable success state for a non-documentation change (see failSafeConditions).
rollbackDesign.auditability: Every PR's selected scope, the specific rule IDs (ESC-##, fullSuiteTriggers entries, or taxonomy defaults) that produced it, and the confidence level must be recorded and retrievable after the fact - not just the pass/fail result. This is a design requirement for any future implementation, not implemented by this task.
